item.title: Trump signs executive order to space out childhood vaccines — What the new plan means
item.description: The move reflects Trump's long-standing view that children should receive vaccines separately rather than getting multiple shots during the same visit.

item.title: RFK Jr’s food crackdown: US FDA proposes stricter food additive rules — What changes for packaged food and consumers?
item.description: Under the proposal, food manufacturers would have to notify the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) before introducing new ingredients through the “generally recognized as safe” (GRAS) pathway.

item.title: Trump rejects Iran’s war compensation demand, seeks counter-payment from Tehran for deaths and injuries
item.description: In a post on Truth Social, Trump said Iranian representatives were seeking compensation for damage caused during the conflict, which he said began because Iran will have to give up its nuclear weapons ambitions.

item.title: Sourav Ganguly, wife Dona receive death threats; Kolkata police begin probe
item.description: Sourav Ganguly and wife Dona received alleged death threats in letters sent over six months. Kolkata Police are tracking a courier trail and mobile number.

item.title: Colombia earthquake: 74 dead as buildings collapse, families dig through rubble for loved ones | In Pics, Videos
item.description: Colombia's Geological Service said it was “the highest magnitude earthquake registered in Colombia in the last decade”.

item.title: Former Meta tech lead shares how he went from DJ to coding before being laid off after 13 years
item.description: His return from paternity leave made the transition particularly challenging. Chen was away from work from August 2025 until towards the end of the year.

item.title: Air India Phuket-Delhi flight incident: French agency BEA, Airbus to assist in AAIB probe
item.description: The teams would be arriving in Delhi on Tuesday.

item.title: LPG under-recoveries of PSU oil firms cross ₹59,000 crore in July
item.description: LPG supplies were among the areas most affected by the war because India relied on West Asia for about 90% of its cooking gas imports before the conflict.

item.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke to launch nationwide social audit of rural government schools on August 15
item.description: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke will launch a nationwide social audit of rural government schools on August 15, urging citizens to check basic facilities and document gaps.

item.title: US visa rule change: Employers to bear ₹3.7 lakh H-1B, ₹4.2 lakh L-1 extension fees; What it means for Indians
item.description: The expanded fee applies to employers with 50 or more employees in the US, provided that more than 50% of their workforce is in H-1B or L-1 nonimmigrant status.

item.title: Low-pressure area seen over northwest Bay of Bengal, heavy rains likely in Odisha: IMD
item.description: The weather agency also forecast isolated heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall over the Western Himalayan region during the week

item.title: William ‘insulted’ after Charles and Camilla reportedly asked Kate to change her name from 'Catherine': Report
item.description: Prince William was reportedly furious when King Charles III and Queen Camilla suggested Kate Middleton change the spelling of her first name to avoid another royal monogram beginning with C, according to a new biography.

item.title: Independence Day 2026: Red Fort to witness first-ever ‘Vande Mataram’ rendition on 15 August
item.description: The celebrations on August 15 will centre on ‘Yuva Shakti’ (youth power) and its role in helping India achieve the goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047, the government said on Monday.

item.title: Lok Sabha passes Tribunals Reforms Bill
item.description: The bill creates a National Tribunals Commission to fill vacancies, review performance and oversee complaints, while leaving NCLT outside its ambit

item.title: Colombia earthquake: Death toll rises to 111, dozens of buildings collapse — latest updates
item.description: The earthquake caused widespread damage in Pereira, Quibdó, Cali and Manizales, while emergency teams and residents searched collapsed structures for survivors.

item.title: Dunkin’ giveaway today? Chain teases possible ‘million’ free-item drop – Know more here
item.description: Dunkin’ fans are speculating about a possible one-million-item giveaway on Monday, 10 August, after a cryptic message in the chain’s Diehards Instagram broadcast channel hinted at a surprise drop.

item.title: Rajya Sabha passes bill to recognize digital bank records as evidence
item.description: The legislation seeks to give electronic banking records legal validity in court while retaining safeguards on their authenticity and integrity.

item.title: Lake Mead water crisis: Why the US reservoir is falling to historic lows
item.description: Lake Mead’s water level reached 1,040.4 feet (317.1 metres) above sea level on Friday (August 7), just below the previous record low set on July 28, 2022.

item.title: K-shaped economy is dead in US? Robert Reich points to McDonald's earnings — ‘Even CEOs are admitting...’
item.description: Robert Reich pushed back against Bessent’s view, saying that the idea that the K-shaped economy is “dead” wrong.

item.title: India expands e-visa network to 88 ports: Check out 11 new immigration points
item.description: The newly designated entry points include nine land ports and two airports. The land ports are Attari along the India-Pakistan border, Darranga, Gede, Ghojadanga, Haridaspur, Jaigaon, Dawki and Moreh. The two airports added to the list are located in Bhopal and Tirupati.

item.title: Will India govt restore Old Pension Scheme? Centre says no proposal under consideration: Here's why
item.description: The Centre has ruled out restoring the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), citing fiscal concerns. Here's why the Modi government prefers NPS and Unified Pension Scheme.

item.title: Bankers' Books Evidence Bill 2026 passed: What the law changes, key takeaways from FM Sitharaman's reply
item.description: Parliament passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, replacing the 1891 law. The Bill recognises electronic, digital and cloud-based banking records as evidence, standardises certification and protects bank officials from unnecessary court summons.

item.title: Govt introduces bill to bar state levies on mining, enhance investor interest
item.description: The government said that the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 aims to reduce the financial burden on mining operations and make them commercially attractive for investments.&nbsp;

item.title: Trump Administration’s ICE detention crackdown puts US courts under severe strain as lawsuits surge nationwide: Report
item.description: The report, based on a review of thousands of ICE detention cases and interviews with detainees, lawyers and judges, found that federal judges have ruled against Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s detention tactics more than 16,000 times over the past year.

item.title: Tupac Shakur murder trial begins today: What to know about the 1996 case, suspect ‘Keffe D’
item.description: Davis is accused of leading a group of men to kill Shakur, 25, one of rap's most commercially successful and influential artists, in a 1996 shooting near the Las Vegas Strip.

item.title: Jailed, deported and in love: How a Japanese man's Bengaluru saga took an unexpected turn
item.description: Tanaka, then a 36-year-old psychology graduate, had come to Bengaluru to learn English and enrolled at a private English academy. He became unhappy after classes were allegedly cancelled frequently and held irregularly.

item.title: Parliament clears taxation bill: FM Sitharaman says UPI will remain free; no framework on MDR yet
item.description: Parliament clears the Taxation Bill as Nirmala Sitharaman says UPI payments will remain free for consumers. No MDR framework has been finalised yet.

item.title: India expands LNG sourcing network from 6 to 15 countries, crude oil from 27 to 41 amid geopolitical risks
item.description: India has expanded its LNG sourcing network from 6 to 15 countries and crude oil sourcing from 27 to 41, the government told Rajya Sabha. The move aims to reduce dependence on specific suppliers and transit routes amid geopolitical risks.

item.title: Crypto Bill heads toward key senate vote in September: What Trump-backed Clarity Act proposes
item.description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune has moved to set up a procedural vote when lawmakers return in mid-September. Republicans will need at least 60 votes, meaning they must win support from at least eight Democrats if all voting Republicans back the bill.

item.title: Earthquake today: 7.4-magnitude quake hits Colombia, 20 buildings collapse in Cali; several trapped
item.description: A morning earthquake shook Colombian capital Bogota on Monday, with the tremor being felt as far away as the border with Venezuela, according to Reuters.

item.title: Zuckerberg’s yacht was closest to stranded boat but ‘refused’ to help: Report
item.description: Zuckerberg's yacht, Launchpad, reportedly did not respond to a stranded skiff's distress call, with the crew unaware due to a different radio channel. The incident garnered attention as a cruise ship ultimately rescued the skiff, raising questions about the yacht's responsiveness.

item.title: Typhoon Dolphin in China: Over 1 million evacuated, flights cancelled, flood alerts issued | What we know so far
item.description: Typhoon Dolphin weakened after making landfall in China’s Zhejiang province, but heavy rain, flooding and landslide risks persisted. Over 1 million people were evacuated, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and transport services disrupted across eastern China.

item.title: Meet the Madhya Pradesh family who loaned ₹35,000 to British govt in 1917 for World War I
item.description: The Ruthia family said they hope that British authorities will be able to check historical records and establish whether the loan was ever repaid or otherwise settled.

item.title: British War Bonds: What is 1917 Indian war loan that MP family invested ₹35,000 in?
item.description: The document shows that businessman Seth Jumma Lal Ruthia, of the firm Seth Rama Kishan Jaskaran Ruthia in princely Bhopal, subscribed ₹35,000 to the Indian War Loan floated by the British government during World War I.

item.title: Lok Sabha passes Tribunals Reforms Bill 2026 amid protests: All about the Bill
item.description: The Lok Sabha passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill 2026 without debate amid Opposition protests. The Bill proposes a National Tribunals Commission, uniform appointment rules and a National Tribunals Data Grid.
